recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: leave-type + employee
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero external dependencies. LeaveType reference data and Employee model are referenced by every downstream module. Build these first so all other modules can import them.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Policy & Cross-cutting: leave-policy + audit + notification
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-policy depends only on leave-type (Phase 1). audit and notification have no module dependencies and are needed by leave-request for GP-002 (audit) and manager notifications. All three can be built in parallel.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Balance engine: leave-balance
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-policy (Phase 2) and employee (Phase 1). The balance module owns the critical deductBalance/restoreBalance transactional logic that leave-request will call during approve/reject/cancel flows.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Orchestration: leave-request
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior phases. This is the orchestration module: submit validates against policy + balance, approve/reject/cancel trigger balance mutations, audit records, and notifications. The controller and routes expose the public API.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Module

### Overview

The leave management module enables employees to apply for annual, sick, and emergency leave. Managers approve or reject requests. The system tracks leave balances and enforces business rules around balance sufficiency, overlapping leaves, and minimum notice periods.

### Domain Entities

- **LeaveType** — reference data for leave categories (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY). Each type defines documentation requirements and maximum consecutive days. Lifecycle: ACTIVE, DEPRECATED.
- **LeavePolicy** — versioned rules per leave type: entitlement, carry-forward limits, notice periods, approval requirements. Lifecycle: ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, REVOKED.
- **LeaveBalance** — per-employee, per-policy, per-fiscal-year tracking of entitled, used, pending, and carried-forward days. Lifecycle: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN.
- **LeaveRequest** — the core application entity. Tracks the full lifecycle from DRAFT → SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED.
- **LeaveStatus** — value object enumerating the states of a LeaveRequest.

### Business Rules

- **BR-001** — Balance Sufficiency: A request may only be submitted if `entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays >= totalDays`.
- **BR-002** — No Overlapping Leaves: An employee cannot have two requests in SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, or APPROVED status with overlapping date ranges.
- **BR-003** — Minimum Notice: A request must be submitted at least `minNoticeDays` before the start date (emergency leave exempt).

### Conceptual Tables

| Table | Key Fields | Notes |
|-------|------------|-------|
| `leave_types` | id, code, label, status | Reference data; indexed on code (unique) and status. |
| `leave_policies` | id, leave_type_id, policy_name, entitlement_days_per_year, min_notice_days, status | Versioned rules; composite index on (leave_type_id, status) for active policy lookup. |
| `leave_requests` | id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, total_days, status, reviewer_id | Core workflow entity; indexed on (employee_id, status) for self-service dashboard, and on dates for overlap detection. |
| `leave_balances` | id, employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days, remaining_days, status | Unique constraint on (employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year). |
| `employees` | id, employee_number, email, manager_id, employment_status | Shared across modules; indexed for manager hierarchy and active status. |
| `audit_logs` | id, entity_type, entity_id, action, performed_by | GP-002 compliance; indexed on (entity_type, entity_id). |
| `notifications` | id, recipient_id, type, status | For notifying employees/managers; indexed on (recipient_id, status). |

### Module Boundaries

```
src/modules/
  leave-type/       — LeaveType model, repository, service, routes
  leave-policy/     — LeavePolicy model, repository, service, routes
  leave-balance/    — LeaveBalance model, repository, service
  leave-request/    — LeaveRequest model, LeaveStatus enum, repository, service, controller, routes
  audit/            — AuditLog model, repository, service
  notification/     — Notification model, repository, service
  employee/         — Employee model, repository, service
```

### Dependency Graph (acyclic)

```
leave-type  ◄── leave-policy  ◄── leave-balance  ◄── leave-request
employee    ◄── leave-balance
employee    ◄── leave-request
leave-type  ◄── leave-request
leave-policy ◄── leave-request
audit       ◄── leave-request
notification ◄── leave-request
```

`leave-request` is the sole outward-facing module; all others are internal dependencies.

### Layer Boundaries

- **Presentation**: Fastify routes + controllers in `leave-request` (the only module exposing HTTP endpoints).
- **Application**: Service interfaces + implementations in each module. `LeaveRequestService` orchestrates `LeavePolicyService`, `LeaveBalanceService`, `AuditService`, `NotificationService`, and `EmployeeService`.
- **Domain**: Models and enums owned by their respective modules.
- **Infrastructure**: PostgreSQL repositories (pg Pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`).

### Golden Principles Compliance

- **GP-001 (Repository pattern)**: Every module has its own repository interface; services call repositories, never raw SQL.
- **GP-002 (Audit records)**: `LeaveRequestService` calls `IAuditService.recordAudit()` on every state change (submit, approve, reject, cancel).
- **GP-003 (Input validation)**: `validateLeaveRequest()` runs before submit; controllers validate DTOs at the boundary.
- **GP-004 (No sensitive data in logs)**: Audit records exclude PII; notification messages carry no sensitive payloads.
- **GP-005 (RBAC enforcement)**: Routes in `leave-request` enforce role checks (employee vs manager vs admin) before delegating to the service.
- **GP-006 (Error handling)**: All async service methods are wrapped; repository errors propagate as typed domain errors.

### Recommended Build Phases

1. **Phase 1 — Foundation**: `leave-type` + `employee` (zero dependencies, referenced by all).
2. **Phase 2 — Policy & Cross-cutting**: `leave-policy` + `audit` + `notification` (parallelizable).
3. **Phase 3 — Balance engine**: `leave-balance` (depends on policy and employee).
4. **Phase 4 — Orchestration**: `leave-request` (depends on all prior phases; exposes the public API).

### Stack

- Language: TypeScript (Node 20)
- Framework: Fastify
- Database: PostgreSQL (via pg Pool)
- Architecture: modular-monolith
- Testing: Jest
sql_schemas: table leave_types | fields: id, code, label, description, requires_documentation, max_consecutive_days, is_paid, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY); status: filtering active leave types for dropdowns and validation

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_id, policy_name, entitlement_days_per_year, max_carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_consecutive_days, requires_approval, effective_from, effective_to, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: looking up all policies for a given leave type; status: filtering active/superseded/revoked policies; leave_type_id, status: dominant access pattern — resolving the active policy for a leave type during request validation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, total_days, reason, status, reviewer_id, reviewer_comment, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; reviewer_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: listing an employee's own leave requests (self-service dashboard); status: filtering by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues, APPROVED/REJECTED for history); employee_id, status: dominant access pattern — employee's requests filtered by status; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; leave_type_id: aggregating leave usage by type for balance calculations

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days, carried_forward_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: looking up an employee's balance across all leave types; employee_id, fiscal_year: dominant access pattern — an employee's balances for the current fiscal year; policy_id: recalculating balances when a policy changes; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint index to prevent duplicate balance records per employee/policy/year

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: listing direct reports for manager approval workflows; employment_status: filtering active employees for leave eligibility; department: grouping employees by department for team calendars

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: looking up audit history for a specific entity (e.g., all changes to a leave request); performed_by: auditing actions by a specific user; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filtering by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE, etc.)

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: listing notifications for a specific user (notification inbox); recipient_id, status: dominant access pattern — unread notifications for a user; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: looking up notifications tied to a specific leave request or balance change
